added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite gate log (neither field is present on the reviewed run's manifest.md, worker.json or supervisor.json), so the added-failure count was not taken.

findings.text: blocking (regression): _head_identity reads the ref file the HEAD names from the checkout's private git directory (git_dir / ref_name), but a linked worktree's refs live in the common git directory named by that directory's `commondir`, so `git_dir / ref_name` does not exist and the identity's ref component is None; _git_directory's docstring claims it 'keeps the HEAD memo working whether the docs tree is served from a main checkout or a worktree', yet in a worktree a new commit leaves the identity unchanged and _git_head returns the stale sha. Reproduced (review-reproduction.log, worktree probe): a linked worktree committed twice; _git_head returned the first head e53b4c2c899a after the second commit whose real HEAD is fdd00a828f20, with identity ((1791668918502012074, 141595810, 20), 'ref: refs/heads/wtb', 'refs/heads/wtb', None) — the ref component None because the worktree's `commondir` is never followed. Because _git_first_committed/_git_last_committed short-circuit on `cached.head == head`, the date maps freeze too. The base (no memo) always ran `git rev-parse HEAD` and was correct there, so this is a staleness the change introduces.

follow-on: _make_repo builds a plain `git init` checkout, so the linked-worktree path the code and its docstring claim to support is never exercised; a regression in the ref resolution (the defect above) keeps the suite green because no test constructs a worktree.
follow-on: _GIT_HEAD_MEMO is keyed on str(repo_dir) and never evicted, so a long-lived server accumulates one entry per checkout path; benign at current scale but unbounded.

follow-on (record-fidelity): the reviewed manifest's tests field carries an unsubstituted `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>` placeholder rather than the literal command that ran; the real command and result are in head-arm.log ('19 passed in 8.57s' / EXIT=0), which I reproduced.
